tara_metadata.item_name: Telematics, OTA Update & ADAS Actuation Subsystem

methodology.impact_rating_method: ISO/SAE 21434 Annex F (Safety, Financial, Operational, Privacy - SFOP)
methodology.attack_feasibility_method: Attack Potential-based Approach (ISO/SAE 21434 Annex G.4 / ISO/IEC 18045)

tree_aggregation_rules.AND_gate: For a complete path, assess all required conditions together. Assign one value to each of the five attack potential factors and sum those values once.
tree_aggregation_rules.OR_gate: Use the lowest score among supported complete paths. If none can be scored, leave the score and feasibility null.

tara_metadata.assessment_status: Initial manual reference for review. The item supplies the impact ratings. Feasibility estimates depend on the stated actor and access assumptions. Residual risk awaits control verification.

threat_scenarios_and_attack_trees.threat_scenario_name: Activation of an altered OTA firmware image

associated_damage_scenario.description: Loss of gateway or brake ECU function can prevent emergency braking when needed. A resulting collision can cause serious injury or death. Loss of ECU function can also prevent vehicle use.

Safety.justification: Loss of gateway or brake ECU function can impair automatic emergency braking and contribute to a fatal collision.

Financial.justification: A collision or ECU repair can cause property and service costs.

Operational.justification: An unavailable ECU can prevent vehicle use.

Privacy.justification: DS-01 identifies no disclosure of personal data.

attack_tree.title: Activation of an altered OTA firmware image

children.title: Altered image presented to a target ECU
children.vulnerability_reference: The TCU OTA agent forwards a staged image without verifying its signature.
children.technical_detail: The agent runs as root. The gateway uses a fixed credential for its own programming. It forwards supported brake diagnostics without checking client authority, and the brake ECU permits programming without a credential. Each target independently rejects incomplete images, wrong-target images and images without a valid trusted signature.

risk_determination.risk_determination_rationale: The proposed image substitution is stopped at activation on both targets. The item establishes neither a failure of this check nor loss of ECU function during rejected or interrupted programming. DS-01 has Severe impact if it occurs. Feasibility and inherent risk remain open.

cybersecurity_goals.description: Reject unauthorized images before forwarding and restrict firmware programming.

cybersecurity_requirements.description: Verify the image signature before forwarding a staged update.
Use individually authorized programming credentials for gateway updates.
Verify client authority before accepting brake ECU programming requests.

proposed_risk_treatment.residual_risk_status: Unassessed pending verification of the proposed controls.

threat_scenarios_and_attack_trees.threat_scenario_name: Incorrect or unavailable automatic emergency braking request

associated_damage_scenario.description: Unintended automatic braking at highway speed can cause a rear-end collision. If automatic emergency braking is unavailable when needed, the vehicle may collide at a higher speed. Either outcome can cause serious injury or death.

Safety.justification: Unintended braking or loss of AEB when needed can contribute to serious or fatal injury.

Financial.justification: A collision can cause vehicle damage and repair costs.

Operational.justification: The vehicle may brake unexpectedly or lose automatic braking assistance.

Privacy.justification: DS-02 identifies no disclosure of personal data.

attack_tree.title: Incorrect or unavailable automatic emergency braking request

children.title: Unauthorized request accepted by the brake ECU
children.vulnerability_reference: The brake ECU checks request format and range but has command MAC verification disabled.
children.technical_detail: COMP-ADAS originates the normal request on CONN-05. COMP-CGW relays it on CONN-04. The TCU diagnostic input provides no raw CAN forwarding. The item establishes no unauthorized sender on either AEB link.

children.title: Interruption of a required AEB request
children.vulnerability_reference: Automatic braking depends on timely requests from the ADAS controller.
children.technical_detail: The gateway relays each request once. The brake ECU holds the last accepted demand until its configured timeout, then clears only AEB demand. A subsequent accepted request restores control. The item identifies no attacker capability to interrupt this flow.

risk_determination.risk_determination_rationale: Both loss of assistance and unintended actuation have defined effects. Access to a local TCU service alone does not establish control over the AEB flow. Feasibility remains open until evidence identifies an actor with the required access.

cybersecurity_goals.description: Protect the source, integrity and availability of the AEB demand.

cybersecurity_requirements.description: Verify the source, integrity and freshness of AEB requests before applying them.
Detect interruption of the AEB input and report loss of the relay function.

proposed_risk_treatment.residual_risk_status: Unassessed pending verification of the proposed controls.

threat_scenarios_and_attack_trees.threat_scenario_name: Unauthorized disclosure of timestamped vehicle location reports

associated_damage_scenario.description: Disclosure of timestamped GPS coordinates can reveal where the vehicle was at a given time. If the vehicle can be linked to a person, multiple reports can reveal that person’s travel patterns and the places they visit.

Safety.justification: The item assigns negligible direct safety impact to disclosure.

Financial.justification: The item assigns Moderate financial impact. Its cost threshold and monetary loss are unspecified.

Operational.justification: Location disclosure alone need not impair vehicle operation.

Privacy.justification: Disclosed reports reveal vehicle locations. Reports linked to a person may reveal travel patterns and places visited.

attack_tree.title: Unauthorized disclosure of timestamped vehicle location reports

children.title: Misuse of an authorized support reader role
children.vulnerability_reference: Authorized OEM support staff can read received reports containing timestamped GPS positions.
children.technical_detail: Actor assumption for this branch: an assigned support reader discloses information already visible to them outside the authorized diagnostic purpose. The staff access interface is unspecified. CONN-01 carries the vehicle upload. Multiple reports and a vehicle-to-person association are required to infer personal travel patterns.
children.scoring_basis: Estimate for an existing support reader. A disclosure during an assigned access window is assumed to take at most a day with ordinary user skill and standard equipment. Internal report knowledge is restricted. Access to relevant reports is assumed to present a moderate opportunity. This estimate applies only to insider misuse.

children.title: Unauthorized reading of the local telemetry queue
children.vulnerability_reference: Pending reports are readable by the TCU telemetry account and root.
children.technical_detail: Acknowledged reports leave the persistent queue. The oldest pending report is discarded when full. Cabin Wi-Fi membership does not grant report access, SSH root login requires a separate workshop key, and the physical serial session has no queue read access. The baseline establishes no unauthorized reader.

risk_determination.risk_determination_rationale: For the stated insider the estimate is 7 (High feasibility). The supplied Major privacy impact gives risk 4 in the project matrix. An external reader acquiring the same access is a separate, unresolved case.

cybersecurity_goals.description: Limit disclosure of location history during diagnostic support.

cybersecurity_requirements.description: Limit support access to reports needed for an assigned case and audit access to identifiable location data.

proposed_risk_treatment.residual_risk_status: Unassessed pending verification of the proposed controls.

traceability_and_risk_summary.assessment_basis: Target checks reject the candidate image. ECU availability during programming is unspecified.
Receiver weakness and timeout behavior are established. An unauthorized path to change or interrupt the demand remains open.

primary_vulnerabilities_exploited: Authorized OEM support staff can read received reports containing timestamped GPS positions.
traceability_and_risk_summary.assessment_basis: Score applies to misuse by an authorized support reader. External access to queued or uploaded reports remains unresolved.
